'''Walter Nazarewicz''' ({{langx|uk|Вальтер Володимир Назаревич|{{transliteration|uk|ukrainian|Valter Volodymyr Nazarevych}}}}) was a Ukrainian-American chemist born on July 18, 1927, in New York.

He came from Derevliani family of Ukrainian immigrants from Dusaniv, a village in Peremyshliany Raion, Lviv Oblast, who arrived to the US in 1916. Nazarewicz studied at the [[Cooper Union]], where he received his undergraduate degree in chemical engineering. 
He then got a master's degree in chemical engineering at [[New York University|NYU]]. 
Once he graduated Nazarewicz joined [[Pfizer]], where he became president of one of its divisions.
Later in life Nazarewicz's career took him to Japan. There he created a subsidiary of Pfizer - Pfizer-Quigley KK - the largest steel industry in the world.

Nazarewicz became a member of the [[Harry F. Sinclair House|Ukrainian Institute of America]], an important center of Ukrainian culture in the US. 
During his presidency at the institute (1981-1999), he did much to encourage new members to join.
In 2007 Nazarewicz spent much time in an effort to modernize a steel plant in [[Mariupol]], Ukraine. He also reconnected with his long lost relatives, who in 1947 were deported from Ukraine to the [[gulag]] in [[Magadan]], Russia.

In honor of his collaboration with [[Bohdan Hawrylyshyn|Bohdan Havrylyshyn]] the [[International Institute for Management Development|International Management Institute]] gave one of their departments his name.
He devoted himself to philanthropy until his death on November 20, 2011.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ukrainianinstitutenyc.wordpress.com/2012/04/02/memorial-concert-in-honor-of-walter-nazarewicz/ | title=Memorial Concert in honor of Walter Nazarewicz | date=2 April 2012 }}</ref>
